ios.desc:
PostPic is a photo-sharing app built around communities and full photo albums.

Find communities around the photography you care about  street photography, film, iPhone photography, portraits, night photography, travel, everyday life and more. Join the ones that match what you shoot, discover albums from other photographers, and share your own work where it belongs.

SHARE COMPLETE PHOTO ALBUMS

A story does not have to be reduced to one photo.

Create albums from your camera roll, arrange your photos in the order you want, add captions, choose a background and keep adding new photos over time.

POST TO PHOTO COMMUNITIES

Share your albums with communities built around particular styles, subjects and ways of shooting.

Browse albums from community members, join conversations and discover photographers beyond the accounts you already follow.

DISCOVER PHOTOGRAPHY

Explore photography from people around the world through complete albums rather than isolated posts.

Whether you are interested in film, street photography, mobile photography, portraits or everyday moments, communities make it easier to find work that matches your interests.

SHOOT WITH POSTPIC

Take photos directly inside PostPic with live effects and film-inspired looks.

Use the PostPic camera when you want to shoot something new, or import photos you already have in your library.

EDIT YOUR PHOTOS

Edit before you publish with tools including:

Presets
Exposure and contrast
Color controls
HSL
Grain
Borders
Film-inspired effects
Halation and bloom
And more

CREATE AND USE RECIPES

Save combinations of edits as recipes so you can reuse a look across different photos.

Discover recipes made by other photographers and apply them to your own work.

BUILD YOUR PHOTOGRAPHIC PROFILE

Your PostPic profile brings together your albums, photography and communities in one place.

Instead of building a profile around individual posts, build a collection of the places, people, subjects and styles you photograph.

PostPic is a place to make photo albums, find photography communities and share your work with people interested in the same things you are.

quotes.text:
We built a place for photography communities.

Something that surprised us while working on this: it's harder than it should be
to find a good home for one online.

Reddit is strong for discussion, and photography there gets treated like any other
post. Discord is great for conversation in the moment, and it gets awkward once
you want to browse or share a large amount of visual work. In both cases the
community is structured around text, and the photos live inside that.

We wanted the photos to be the structure.

So we built an app where anyone can create a community around a photography niche,
customize it, set their own rules, and invite people with a shareable link.
Communities are organized around albums for now. You can make something broad like
street photography, or narrow like 35mm shot in Paris, and let it grow from there.

Members post as many photos as they want, explore other niches, and find people
shooting the same things they are. There's a camera and editor built in too, with
effects written in Metal running on the GPU in real time, and filters you can
export as recipes and share with others.

We're leaving most of the structure to the people creating the communities rather
than deciding up front what a photography community should look like.

If you're part of one today, on Reddit, Discord, Facebook groups, Flickr, anywhere:
what do you find frustrating about it?
